name: Coralbell
lede: Coralbell is a dark yellowish pink from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, named for the coral bells flower, and closest in our library to terracotta.

sections.title: A flower on a 1930 plate
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's *A Dictionary of Color* dates this hue to 1928, on plate 3, cell H10 [1]. Coral bells (*Heuchera*) is a garden perennial with small, bell-shaped pink-red flowers on tall stalks, and the dictionary's name follows that plant, though it does not spell out the exact flower variety meant [1]. The ISCC-NBS 1955 report classes the color as a moderate red [2].

The nearest named colors on file are [[strawberry-pink]], [[light-jasper-red]], [[brownish-pink]] and [[antique-pink]], at 3.5, 4.9, 5.2 and 5.3 ΔE [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: ColorHub's archive finds this color in 55 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.2 percent, as photographed [4]. The match peaks in the 1910s, in 6 of 523 paintings, with hits spread across Nepal, Iran, Austria and Tibet rather than clustered in one tradition [4]. The count is a computed color match on photographed, varnished canvases, not a pigment identification [4].
